mainTopic: Carrying beyond one's תחום (זריקה versus משיכה), the pen and stable dispute, and why a boat is treated leniently
overview: This amud continues the discussion of רב הונא's view that a person may not throw objects into an area where he himself may not walk. A ברייתא seems to permit carrying throughout a city even when the person's limit ends in the middle of it. רב הונא answers that this means pulling objects toward himself, not throwing. רב הונא adds that if the limit ends mid-courtyard, the person may still carry in his half, and we do not worry that he will carry in the rest. רב נחמן says that even רב הונא permits carrying throughout a house when the limit ends at the roof's edge, because the roof edge acts like a wall. רב הונא בריה דרב נתן tries to link the dispute to the משנה about a person placed in a pen or stable, but the גמרא rejects both sides of that comparison. רב rules like רבן גמליאל in a pen, a stable, and a boat, while שמואל rules like him only on a boat. רבה and רבי זירא give different reasons why a boat is lenient. The גמרא begins to explain why רבי זירא rejects רבה's reason, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a limit that ends mid-city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. If a person's תחום measurement ends in the middle of a city, he may carry throughout the whole city but may not walk past his limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person was measuring his שבת limit and the measurement ran out halfway through a city, he may carry throughout the entire city, as long as he does not walk past the limit on his own feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the setup for a challenge against רב הונא. This step only states the source; the attack comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person measured his 2,000 אמות from his עירוב, and the measurement ended in the middle of a city. The ברייתא allows him to 'carry' in the whole city but forbids his body from crossing the line. So objects may reach places where he himself may not go.

keyTerms.meaning: was measuring as he went (his 2,000 אמות)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of limits here. The person's body may not leave his תחום, but the ברייתא is talking about objects moving across the city. The whole question is how those objects get there.

phrases.english: If he was measuring as he went,
phrases.notes: Measuring his 2,000 cubits from the spot of his עירוב.

phrases.english: and his measurement ended in the middle of the city —
he is permitted to carry throughout the entire city,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲבוֹר אֶת הַתְּחוּם בְּרַגְלָיו.
phrases.english: provided that he does not cross the limit with his feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה מוֹדֵד וּבָא, וְכָלְתָה מִדָּתוֹ בַּחֲצִי הָעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא as the basis for challenging רב הונא's earlier view in the sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a person's limit ends mid-city, he may carry in the whole city but may not walk past his limit.

steps.title: Does carrying here mean throwing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how he could carry into areas he cannot walk to. It must be by throwing, which contradicts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'carry' mean here? Isn't it by throwing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the ברייתא to attack רב הונא. Carrying into a place you cannot walk to seems to mean throwing objects there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא forbids moving objects by זריקה into a place where the person himself may not walk. The concern is that he may go after them. If the ברייתא allows carrying in the whole city, that seems to permit exactly the throwing רב הונא forbids.

phrases.english: What does 'he carries' mean?
Is it not by means of throwing?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מְטַלְטֵל, לָאו עַל יְדֵי זְרִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a hostile inference from the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's prohibition on throwing objects into an area where one may not walk.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only apparent way to carry into the forbidden half is throwing, and the ברייתא permits it.

steps.title: רב הונא: it means pulling, not throwing
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that 'carrying' in the ברייתא means pulling objects toward himself, not throwing them away from himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: No, it means by pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself. He rereads the ברייתא as referring to משיכה, drawing objects in toward himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he pulls an object from the far side of the city into his permitted area, the object comes to him. So there is no worry that he will walk after it. Throwing sends an object away from him, and that is where the worry applies.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
No, by means of pulling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לָא, עַל יְדֵי מְשִׁיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Carry' in the ברייתא means throwing into the forbidden area.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Carry' means pulling objects into the permitted area, so it does not contradict רב הונא.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא survives the challenge. Pulling an object toward yourself is fine. Throwing it into a place you may not walk is not.

steps.title: רב הונא: a limit ending mid-courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that if one's measurement ends in the middle of a courtyard, he has only half the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If he was measuring and his measurement ended in the middle of a courtyard, he has only half the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a new, related rule. This time the limit ends in the middle of a חצר instead of a city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard is one enclosed space, so one might think it counts as a single unit. רב הונא says the line of the תחום still splits it. The person gets only the half that falls inside his limit.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
If he was measuring as he went,
and his measurement ended in the middle of a courtyard —
he has only half the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הָיָה מוֹדֵד וּבָא, וְכָלְתָה מִדָּתוֹ בַּחֲצִי חָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to the city case, now about a courtyard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the limit ends mid-courtyard, he has only the half inside his limit.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this is obvious. Of course a person cannot walk beyond his תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's rule as saying nothing new. Everyone knows you cannot go past your limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's statement should teach a חידוש, something new. Saying he 'has only half' the courtyard just repeats the basic rule of תחום. So the גמרא asks what רב הונא is adding.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב הונא's statement in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that he has only half the courtyard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being limited by one's תחום is basic and needs no teaching.

steps.title: Read it as: he does have half the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רב הונא positively. His point is that the person does have the use of half the courtyard, including carrying there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: he has half the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רב הונא's statement so that it teaches something new. The point is what he is allowed to do, not what he is forbidden to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is a permission. He may carry in his half of the courtyard. One might have thought that since the other half is forbidden, his half should be restricted too. The גמרא will go on to explain why someone might have thought otherwise.

phrases.english: Say: he has half the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: יֵשׁ לוֹ חֲצִי חָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 5 by rewording step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא was restricting the person to half the courtyard, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא was granting the person the use of half the courtyard, including carrying there.
steps.whatToRemember: The same words can be read as a limit ('only half') or as a permission ('he has half'). The גמרא picks the reading that teaches something new: he may use and carry in his half.

steps.title: Isn't this also obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges even the new reading of רב הונא as too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this also obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 6 explained that רב הונא lets the person use half the courtyard. Now the גמרא asks why רב הונא needed to say even that, since it seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person may walk in half the courtyard, it seems natural that he may also carry there. So the positive reading of רב הונא still seems to add nothing. The גמרא is pushing to find the real new point.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. Used to ask why a teaching was needed at all.
This too. It signals that a second statement is being challenged, just like the first.

phrases.english: Is this too obvious?
phrases.notes: 'Too' refers back to step 5, where the first reading was also called obvious.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי נָמֵי פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the positive reading of רב הונא given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רב הונא in step 6, that the person may carry in half the courtyard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carrying within an area where one may walk is obviously allowed, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The concern that he will carry in the whole courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא needed to teach this because we might have feared the person would carry in the entire courtyard, so we would forbid carrying even in his half.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us be worried that he will come to carry in the whole courtyard. So רב הונא teaches us that we are not worried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 7. רב הונא is teaching us that we do not worry the person will spill over into the forbidden half of the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard looks like one open space with no wall in the middle. So we could have thought חכמים would forbid carrying even in the allowed half, as a fence against carrying in the rest. רב הונא tells us this extra restriction does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. It introduces the mistaken thought that the teaching comes to remove.
Let us be concerned. It raises a possible protective worry.
It teaches us. This is the new point of the teaching.

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's ruling has two parts. The person cannot go past his half of the courtyard. But he may fully use his half, including carrying, and we do not worry he will carry in the rest.

phrases.english: You might have said:
Let us be concerned that perhaps he will come to carry in all of it,
phrases.notes: 'All of it' means the whole courtyard, including the half outside his limit.

phrases.english: So he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a non-obvious point (מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would forbid carrying even in the permitted half, as a fence against carrying in the whole courtyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such fence is made. He may carry in his half of the courtyard.

steps.title: רב נחמן: when the limit ends at the edge of a roof
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that רב הונא agrees with him in one case. If a person's limit ends exactly at the edge of a house's roof, he may carry throughout the whole house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: הונא agrees with me in this case. If a person was measuring his limit and his measurement ended at the edge of a roof, he may carry in the whole house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a new case where even רב הונא agrees that carrying is allowed. Most of the house is beyond the person's limit, yet he may carry throughout it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא is usually strict. He worries a person who carries into a place where he cannot walk may follow his object there. Here רב נחמן says רב הונא admits carrying is allowed, by throwing, into the whole house, even though most of it is beyond the limit.

keyTerms.meaning: He agrees with me. One אמורא claims his opponent concedes a certain case.
Was measuring as he went. He was counting out his 2000 אמות.

steps.confusionAlert: The house is mostly outside the person's limit. He still may not walk past the roof edge. The ruling is only about carrying objects into the house, by throwing.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, מוֹדֶה לִי הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Huna agrees with me:
If he was measuring as he went,
phrases.notes: He is counting his 2000 אמות from his עירוב.

phrases.english: and his measurement ended at the edge of a roof,
he is permitted to carry throughout the whole house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, מוֹדֶה לִי הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the courtyard case to a related case where רב הונא's usual strictness does not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the limit ends at the edge of a roof, one may carry throughout the house, and even רב הונא agrees.

steps.title: Why does רב הונא agree here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason רב הונא agrees in the roof case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב הונא, who is usually strict, allows carrying in this house. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a reason, the roof case would seem to contradict רב הונא's worry that a person will follow his object. The גמרא wants to know what makes this case different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the logic behind רב נחמן's claim in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב הונא permits carrying throughout the house in the roof case.

steps.title: The roof edge acts like a wall
steps.stepSummary: The edge of the roof is seen as if it presses straight down, forming a wall at the end of his limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the roof of the house presses down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the edge of the roof counts like a wall coming down at the exact spot where the limit ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the roof edge is treated as a wall, there is a clear barrier at the end of his limit. With that barrier, there is no worry that he will wander past it after his object. This is why רב הונא agrees here but not in an open area.

keyTerms.meaning: Presses down. The roof edge is viewed as coming straight down and closing off the space.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the root of רב הונא's strictness. He is concerned only where nothing marks the boundary. A wall-like barrier, even one we only picture, removes the worry.

phrases.english: Since the roof of the house presses down.
phrases.notes: The roof edge is viewed as a wall coming down to the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְתִקְרַת הַבַּיִת חוֹבֶטֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The roof edge is treated as a wall pressing down, which forms a barrier at the end of the limit. So there is no fear he will follow his object.

steps.title: The argument matches an argument among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן says the argument about carrying matches an argument in the משנה. The case there is a person taken by force to another city and placed in a pen or stable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב נתן, said: this is like an argument among תנאים. If they took him to another city and placed him in a pen or a stable, רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה say he may walk in all of it. רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא say he has only four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא says the earlier argument about carrying past one's area is not new. It matches an older argument among תנאים in the משנה. The גמרא will next work out how the two arguments line up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a person was taken by non-Jews outside his limit and placed in an enclosed pen or stable. רבן גמליאל treats the whole enclosed area like four אמות, so he may walk in all of it. רבי יהושע gives him only four אמות from where he was placed. רב הונא בריה דרב נתן suggests this matches the argument between רב הונא and the lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like a dispute of תנאים. An argument among אמוראים is matched to an earlier argument among תנאים.
A pen, an enclosure for animals.
A stable or animal enclosure surrounded by a fence.
Four אמות, the small area a person may always move in, even outside his limit.
He may walk in all of it, the whole enclosure.

steps.confusionAlert: This is a quote from a משנה earlier in the פרק, brought here for comparison. The גמרא has not yet said which תנא matches which אמורא. That comes next.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said:
phrases.notes: This is a different person from the רב הונא discussed earlier.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute of Tannaim.
If they took him to another city,
phrases.notes: 'They' are non-Jews who took him by force, outside his limit.

phrases.english: and placed him in a pen or a stable,

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya say:
He may walk in all of it.
phrases.notes: The enclosed area counts like four אמות.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva say:
He has only four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן: כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the roof case and links the main argument about carrying to an earlier argument among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between אמוראים about carrying matches the argument in the משנה about a person placed in a pen or stable. One side lets him walk in the whole enclosure, and the other gives only four אמות.

steps.title: The lenient תנאים do not decree carrying because of walking
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה let the person walk through the whole pen. So they do not forbid walking in the pen out of fear he will walk in an open field. If they do not even decree walking because of walking, they surely would not decree carrying because of walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it true that רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who say he may walk through the entire area, do not forbid walking in a pen or stable because of walking in an open field? And since they do not forbid one kind of walking because of another kind of walking, they would not forbid carrying because of walking.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן now explains how the משנה's dispute matches the carrying dispute. He starts with the lenient side, רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, these תנאים let the person walk anywhere inside the enclosed pen. They are not worried that he will get used to it and walk freely in an open field, where he is limited to 4 אמות. The reasoning is that if they won't decree walking because of walking, which is a very similar act, they certainly won't decree carrying because of walking, which is a different act.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (introduces a proposed explanation or proof)
They decree (make a rabbinic safeguard prohibition)
Because of / out of concern for
An animal pen and a stable (enclosed areas)

steps.confusionAlert: Walking and carrying are two different acts here. The question is whether we forbid carrying, which would normally be allowed, out of fear that the person will come to walk where he may not. Don't mix up which act is being forbidden and which act is the concern.

phrases.english: Is it not that

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
who said: he may walk through all of it,
do not decree against walking in a pen or stable
because of walking in an open field;
and since they do not decree walking because of walking,
phrases.notes: This is building up to an 'all the more so' argument.

phrases.english: they do not decree carrying because of walking.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו, רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה דְּאָמְרוּ: מְהַלֵּךְ אֶת כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא בריה דרב נתן's comparison, which was introduced in step 12, by explaining the lenient side of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The view that does not decree carrying because of walking (the view opposing רב הונא)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allow walking in the whole pen or stable

steps.title: The strict תנאים do decree carrying because of walking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא limit the person to 4 אמות even inside the pen. So they do forbid walking in the pen out of concern about walking in an open field. It follows that they would also forbid carrying out of concern about walking, which is רב הונא's position.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא, who say he has only four אמות, decree against walking in a pen or stable because of walking in an open field. Since they decree walking because of walking, they also decree carrying because of walking.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the comparison continues with the strict side of the משנה. It shows that רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא hold the same way as רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the pen is enclosed, these תנאים give the person only 4 אמות. They fear he will treat an open field the same way. Since they are willing to make a safeguard decree here, it follows that they would also forbid carrying because of walking, just like רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, the small area a person outside his limit may move in

steps.whatToRemember: The full comparison: the lenient תנאים do not decree carrying because of walking, and the strict תנאים (רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא) do decree it, like רב הונא.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva, who say:
he has only four cubits,
decree against walking in a pen or stable
because of walking in an open field;
and since they decree walking because of walking,
they also decree carrying because of walking.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּאוֹמְרִים: אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the strict side of the same comparison, as the mirror image of step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that carrying is forbidden because of walking
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא limit the person to 4 אמות in the pen or stable

steps.title: The lenient תנאים may only be lenient because the pen and field are separate places
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. Maybe רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה did not decree only because the pen and the open field are two different places. So their leniency proves nothing about a decree within one single place.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps when רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה did not decree walking in a pen or stable because of walking in an open field, that applies only there, because they are two separate places.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison it just made. It suggests the lenient תנאים had a narrower reason for their leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pen is enclosed by walls, and the open field is a completely different place. There is little reason to worry that a person will confuse them, so no decree is needed. That logic says nothing about a case within one area, so these תנאים might still agree with רב הונא there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a leniency in one case does not automatically carry over to another case. The reason behind the leniency, here the fact that there are two distinct places, may limit how far it applies.

phrases.english: From where (do you know)?
Perhaps when they did not decree,

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
against walking in a stable or pen
because of walking in an open field,
that applies only there,
because they are two separate places.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא כִּי לָא גָּזְרִי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 13 about the lenient תנאים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה would never decree carrying because of walking
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Their leniency may rest on the pen and the field being two distinct places, a reason that does not apply within one area.

steps.title: Even רבן גמליאל might decree carrying within one place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its first rejection. When carrying and walking happen in the same place, even רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה might decree, because a person may follow his object.
steps.simpleTranslation: But carrying because of walking, where it is all one place, maybe they would decree, out of concern that he will be drawn after his object.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the rejection from Step 15. It says that רבן גמליאל might be lenient only when there are two separate places. When everything is in one place, he might also decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pen case, the pen and the open field are two different places, so a decree there would be far-fetched. In the carrying case, the object lands in the same area where the person might walk. That creates a real risk that he goes after his object. So even רבן גמליאל could agree with רב הונא's decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest he be drawn after his object

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not say רבן גמליאל definitely decrees. It only says he might, so his leniency in the pen proves nothing about רב נחמן's position.

phrases.english: But carrying because of walking
where it is one place
indeed, they would also decree
a decree lest he be drawn after his object.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל טִלְטוּל אַטּוּ הִילּוּךְ דְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in Step 15 by stating the other half of the distinction.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה for רב נחמן's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A pen and a field are two places, but carrying and walking can happen in one place, where a decree is more reasonable.

steps.title: רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא may not be decreeing at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the other side of the comparison. רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא may limit the person to 4 אמות for a different reason: a house counts as 4 אמות only if he was inside its walls before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא, how do we know their reason is a decree? Maybe they hold that the rule 'a whole house counts as 4 אמות' applies only when he settled inside the walls while it was still day. Where he did not settle inside the walls while it was still day, it does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the proof from Step 14. It suggests a different reason for רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא's strictness that has nothing to do with decrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an enclosed space counts like 4 אמות, so a person may walk all of it. That rule may apply only if the person was within the walls when שבת began. The person in the pen was brought there after שבת started, so he simply gets 4 real אמות. That is a basic rule, not a decree, so it tells us nothing about רב הונא's decree on carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, the basic personal space on שבת
Here: established his שבת place of rest
While it was still day, before שבת began

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs are rejected, so the argument between רב הונא and רב נחמן is not the same as the תנאים' argument about the pen.
steps.whyThisMatters: It introduces an important idea: an enclosed space counts as 4 אמות only if one was there before שבת. That idea helps explain the halachic rulings that follow.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva too
from where do we know it is because they decree?
Perhaps it is because they hold
that when we say the entire house
is considered like four cubits
this applies only where he established his place
within the airspace of walls while it was still day.
But where he did not establish his place
within the airspace of walls while it was still day, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נָמֵי מִמַּאי דְּמִשּׁוּם דְּגָזְרִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having rejected the proof from רבן גמליאל's side, the גמרא now rejects the proof from רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא for רב הונא's view, and with it the whole comparison made by רב הונא בריה דרב נתן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Their strictness may come from a basic rule about when walls count as 4 אמות, not from any decree.

steps.title: רב rules like רבן גמליאל in pen, stable, and boat
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל in all three cases: a pen, a stable, and a boat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The הלכה is like רבן גמליאל regarding a pen, a stable, and a boat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves from analysis to a practical ruling. רב says we follow רבן גמליאל's lenient view in every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, a person may walk through the entire enclosed space in all three cases, even if he was brought there by force. He does not distinguish between the pen and stable on one side and the boat on the other.

phrases.english: Rav said:
The halacha is like Rabban Gamliel
regarding a pen, a stable, and a boat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הִלְכְתָא כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the comparison is rejected, the גמרא turns to the practical הלכה in the תנאים' dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל in a pen, a stable, and a boat, so one may walk through the entire space.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבן גמליאל only on a boat
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. He follows רבן גמליאל only on a boat, not in a pen or stable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The הלכה is like רבן גמליאל regarding a boat, but not regarding a pen or a stable.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a narrower ruling than רב. He is lenient on a boat but strict in a pen or stable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל splits the cases: on a boat the person may walk the whole boat, but in a pen or stable he gets only 4 אמות. שמואל himself gives no reason here. The גמרא asks next why everyone agrees about the boat, and רבה and רבי זירא give two different reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: And שמואל said, introducing a disagreeing view
No, the הלכה does not follow him there

steps.whatToRemember: רב: like רבן גמליאל in pen, stable, and boat. שמואל: like רבן גמליאל only on a boat.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
The halacha is like Rabban Gamliel regarding a boat,
but regarding a pen and a stable, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר הִלְכְתָא כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּסְפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing, narrower ruling to רב's ruling in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל only on a boat. In a pen or stable, the person is limited to 4 אמות.

steps.title: Why does everyone agree about the boat?
steps.stepSummary: Both רב and שמואל rule like רבן גמליאל about a boat. The גמרא asks what makes the boat different.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, everyone agrees that the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל on a boat. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out the one case where רב and שמואל agree, the boat, and asks why it is different. This sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב follows רבן גמליאל in all three cases, and שמואל follows him only on a boat. So the boat is common ground. The question is what reason makes a boat more lenient than a pen or a stable.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone; all opinions agree (here, both רב and שמואל)
At any rate; in any case

phrases.english: In any case, everyone agrees
phrases.notes: Everyone here means both רב and שמואל.

phrases.english: that the halacha follows Rabban Gamliel on a boat,
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּסְפִינָה, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the shared point of רב and שמואל and asks for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the boat is treated more leniently than the pen and the stable.

steps.title: רבה: He settled inside the boat's walls before שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the boat is different because the person began שבת inside its walls, so the whole boat counts as his 4 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Because he settled for שבת inside the area of the walls while it was still day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the first reason. The person was already inside the boat's walls when שבת began, so the whole walled boat counts like his 4 אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the idea from step 17: an enclosed area counts as 4 אמות only if he was inside its walls before שבת. A person on a boat was inside the walls from the start. So the boat's walls are the key, according to רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: He settled for שבת (his place of rest was set)
While it was still day, before שבת began

phrases.english: Rabba said:
since he settled for Shabbat within the area of walls
phrases.notes: Meaning the walls of the boat.

phrases.english: while it was still day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: הוֹאִיל וְשָׁבַת בַּאֲוִיר מְחִיצּוֹת מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The boat is lenient because the person was inside its walls before שבת began.

steps.title: רבי זירא: The boat keeps moving him anyway
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the boat is different because it keeps carrying the person out of his 4 אמות, so limiting him to 4 אמות makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Because the boat picks him up from the start of 4 אמות and puts him down at the end of 4 אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a different reason. The moving boat keeps shifting the person out of any 4 אמות, so he may walk around the whole boat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי זירא, the walls are not the point. The point is that the boat's motion means he could never stay in one fixed 4 אמות even if he tried. So there is no reason to limit his walking on the boat.

keyTerms.meaning: It picks him up; carries him
Four cubits, the basic area a person may move in on שבת

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
since the boat picks him up from the beginning of four cubits
and puts him down at the end of four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר: הוֹאִיל וּסְפִינָה נוֹטַלְתּוֹ מִתְּחִילַּת אַרְבַּע וּמַנַּחְתּוֹ בְּסוֹף אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The boat is lenient because its movement keeps taking him out of his 4 אמות anyway.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what case the reasons of רבה and רבי זירא would lead to different rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever give a different result. This sets up the next step, which gives the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons explain the same ruling about a normal boat. The גמרא wants a case where only one of the reasons still applies, so we can see that they really differ.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? (a request for a practical case where they differ)

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where רבה's reason and רבי זירא's reason give different rulings.

steps.title: Two cases: broken walls, or jumping to another boat
steps.stepSummary: The reasons differ when the boat's walls break, or when the person jumps from one boat to another. רבה's reason no longer works there, but רבי זירא's still does.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when the boat's walls were broken. Or also: when a person jumps from one boat to another boat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two cases where the reasons split. In both, the walls he settled in are gone or left behind, but the boat still moves him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the walls break, he is no longer inside walls, so רבה's reason fails, but the boat still moves him, so רבי זירא lets him walk the whole boat. If he jumps to a different boat, he did not settle inside its walls before שבת, so רבה's reason fails again, but רבי זירא's reason still applies on the new moving boat.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: the boat is lenient because of its walls, where he settled before שבת. רבי זירא: it is lenient because the boat keeps moving him. So with broken walls or a jump to another boat, only רבי זירא's reason still works.
steps.confusionAlert: Both cases are not two separate arguments. They are two examples of the same difference: the walls he settled in are missing, but the boat is still moving.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where the walls of the boat were breached.
phrases.notes: He is no longer inside walls, so רבה's reason does not apply.

phrases.english: Alternatively:
with one who jumps from boat to boat.
phrases.notes: He did not settle in the new boat's walls before שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ שֶׁנִּפְחֲתוּ דּוֹפְנֵי סְפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 with two practical cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ when the boat's walls broke, or when he jumped to another boat. רבה's reason fails, but רבי זירא's still applies.

steps.title: Why does רבי זירא not agree with רבה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי זירא did not explain the boat case the way רבה did, using the boat's walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רבי זירא, what is the reason he did not say like רבה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי זירא did not give the same reason as רבה. This question sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains רבי זירא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's reason is simple: the person began שבת inside the boat's walls, so the whole boat counts as his 4 אמות. So why would רבי זירא need a different reason? The גמרא wants to know what problem רבי זירא sees in רבה's approach.

keyTerms.meaning: Like רבה (the same as רבה's opinion)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira,
phrases.notes: The גמרא turns its focus to רבי זירא.

phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say like Rabbah?
phrases.notes: רבה's reason (the walls) seems simpler, so why not use it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי זֵירָא, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the practical difference between the two reasons has been shown in step 24, the גמרא asks why רבי זירא rejects רבה's reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי זירא's objection to the reasoning that the boat's walls make the whole boat one's 4 אמות?

steps.title: רבי זירא's answer begins with the boat's walls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer on behalf of רבי זירא: the problem is with the boat's walls (מחיצות). The full explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: The walls...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to explain רבי זירא's view and points to the boat's walls as the issue. The sentence is not finished here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's whole reason depends on the boat's walls counting as real walls that define a living space. By opening with the word מחיצות, the גמרא signals that רבי זירא disagrees with that very point. Some explain that the sides of a boat are not considered proper partitions. The reason why comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (the גמרא explains what this אמורא would answer)
Walls or partitions, which can define an enclosed area in הלכה

steps.confusionAlert: This answer is not finished on this amud. Do not stop at the word מחיצות. The next passage explains what is wrong with the boat's walls.

phrases.english: He could say to you: The walls,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud. The point is that a boat's walls do not count as proper partitions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: מְחִיצּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question of step 25 by beginning to attack the basis of רבה's reason, which is the walls.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי זירא disagrees with רבה because he does not consider the boat's walls to be proper partitions. The full reason continues on the next amud.
